## Lisbon Apartment Snapshot for Remote Work

You have a **EUR 1,500/month** ceiling and a **12-month lease**, so all three options fit on rent alone. For your priorities, the key trade-off is between **quiet nights**, **internet reliability**, and **daily walkability**.

## Ranked Comparison: Quiet, Connectivity, and Walkability

| Option | Area | Type | Size | Rent | Commute | Fit for Priorities |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | **Avenidas Novas** | 1-bedroom | 52 m² | **EUR 1,500** | 15 min by metro | **Best overall** |
| 2 | **Campo de Ourique** | Studio | 40 m² | **EUR 1,200** | 20 min by bus | **Best value** |
| 3 | **Alfama** | 1-bedroom | 48 m² | **EUR 1,350** | 25 min by tram | **Least aligned** |

## Why This Ranking Works

### 1) Avenidas Novas — Best overall
- **Quiet at night:** Usually the strongest fit here; it is more residential and less nightlife-heavy than central historic areas.
- **Reliable internet:** Best odds of stable building stock and better telecom infrastructure than older, denser neighborhoods.
- **Walkability:** Very good for daily errands, cafes, and services; also easy metro access.
- **Trade-off:** It uses your full housing budget, leaving less room for utilities or upgrades.

### 2) Campo de Ourique — Best value
- **Quiet at night:** Strong fit; generally calmer than Alfama.
- **Reliable internet:** Good, though exact reliability still depends on the building and provider.
- **Walkability:** Excellent neighborhood feel with shops, cafes, and daily needs close by.
- **Trade-off:** It is a **studio**, so space for a dedicated work area is the main limitation.

### 3) Alfama — Least aligned
- **Quiet at night:** Weakest fit; tourist traffic, narrow streets, and evening activity can make it less restful.
- **Reliable internet:** Older housing stock can be a risk for wiring and signal quality.
- **Walkability:** Very walkable, but often in a more crowded, tourist-oriented way than a practical everyday-neighborhood way.
- **Trade-off:** Charming location, but not the best match for focused remote work.

## Decision Criteria That Matter Most

- **Quiet at night:** Prioritize residential streets, higher floors, double glazing, and non-touristy blocks.
- **Reliable internet:** Ask for actual fiber provider, speed test results, and router setup before signing.
- **Walkability:** Look for groceries, cafes, pharmacies, and transit within a 5–10 minute walk.
- **Work-from-home comfort:** A separate desk area matters more than raw square meters if you work full-time from home.
- **Budget flexibility:** Staying below EUR 1,500 can help cover utilities, internet, and occasional coworking.
